subject: Control page (.private/control.html, generated by tools/build-control.py) — full review of the shipped state, post 4-seat run
review_level: screen-component (one surface, built), with a flow check on the page→terminal handoff
privacy_note: This file is TRACKED in a PUBLIC repo. It carries no deviceId, no ribbon text, no verbatim of Mom's, and no engagement figure attributable to a person. Quotes below are structural strings and tool output only. That constraint is deliberate and is the same rule the charter set for itself.
method: Read the rendered instance built 2026-08-06 10:43 AM ET (NOT the 08-04 one the spec reviewed — the page has been rebuilt and most seat-2 findings are fixed). Read build-control.py in full, mom-cycle-status.py's LEGS/gather/position/main, the seat-1 charter, the seat-2 spec, Fernwood CLAUDE.md, and cross-project/ordering-and-layout.md. records_finding: No seat-4 review artifact exists in .ux-reviews/. Its items (D1–D6, D16) survive only as inline comments in build-control.py. A review whose only copy is a code comment cannot be re-read against the artifact later, and cannot be audited for what was deliberately left unfixed — which is exactly what this review had to reconstruct. Recommend writing the seat-4 findings out as a JSON alongside the spec.

user_context.primary_user: Paul, alone, and only Paul-the-operator-of-a-loop. Never Mom. Mom's accessibility doctrine (icon+size+color+position, consistency-over-precision) is OUT OF SCOPE here and was not applied.

D2 Is she being shown something wrong right now?

Screenshot clipping was reported at 'a 1200px window'. I could not reproduce a viewport measurement; F8 states exactly which widths clip and why, and names what to check if 1200 is literal.

scope_decisions.does_fernwood_tone_doctrine_apply: SPLIT — and this is a deliberate call, not a hedge. The PALETTE half does NOT apply. Red/green pills, WANTS YOU, the red verdict band and the ops register are legitimate here and are the correct reading of the Fernwood candidate principle 'Register is carried by chrome, not just words' — whose own corollary reads: 'no ops-chrome on LIVING-PROPERTY surfaces, NOT everything must look like the journal.' A reviewer who gutted the red/green here would be applying viewer.html's rules to a surface built to be visually incapable of being mistaken for viewer.html, which is the generator's stated purpose. The MECHANISM half DOES apply. The anti-urgency rule's real content is 'a red that never means anything trains the reader to ignore red' — the charter states it in its own words as the reason the monitor moment was rejected. On this page, `Unpushed 3` renders red on most visits while the band above it stays green (F1). That is the mechanism failing, in ops clothing. Import the mechanism, not the palette.
scope_decisions.is_the_page_the_right_shape: Yes. The macro structure is right and a generic reviewer would wrongly attack it — see correct_as_is.

the_headline_defect_diagnosed.what_paul_observed: Top verdict reads 'Nothing is waiting on you' while check-data-inline.py and check-digest-fresh.py both render WANTS YOU further down.
the_headline_defect_diagnosed.is_it_an_aggregation_bug: NO. The verdict DOES consider the canon checks. verdict() routes canon_surfaces into a second tier (`notes`) and prints it in line2; mom-cycle-status.position() likewise returns leg 5 precisely BECAUSE canon is dirty. Nothing is excluded and nothing is silently dropped. The two-tier model — owed-to-Mom vs. owed-by-you-but-not-to-her — is a real and defensible distinction and should survive.
the_headline_defect_diagnosed.is_it_a_labelling_bug: YES, and this is the primary diagnosis. The model has two tiers; the vocabulary has one. 'Nothing is waiting on you' is an ABSOLUTE about Paul's whole queue, used to name a tier that only means 'nothing is owed to Mom.' The subline then has to retract it with the word 'also:'. A headline whose own subline names an exception has already failed as a headline. Every mixed run — the common run — will produce this contradiction, because the words guarantee it.
the_headline_defect_diagnosed.is_it_conceptual: PARTLY, and the conceptual part is smaller than it looks but sharper. 'Waiting on you' in the charter's own framing (D1: 'is any of it mine?') means anything Paul and only Paul will fix. Canon drift and three unpushed commits both qualify — nobody else will do them. They are not owed TO HER; they are still HIS. So the tier boundary is correctly drawn (owed-to-her vs. not) and incorrectly named (waiting-on-you vs. nothing).
the_headline_defect_diagnosed.the_worse_sibling_i_found: See F1. There is a second, cleaner instance of the same class where the verdict does NOT consider the input at all, because the branch is unreachable code. That one is worse than the canon case Paul spotted.

findings.observation: The verdict's unpushed/dirty branch is DEAD CODE and can never fire. verdict() reads `repo = sig.get("repo") or {}` and then `if repo.get("unpushed_commits")` / `if repo.get("dirty_files")` — but gather() constructs `sig` with exactly three keys (served_queue, return_leg, canon_surfaces) and never a `repo` key. mom-cycle-status.gather() DOES populate `repo`, but build-control deliberately calls only CYCLE.position(sig), never CYCLE.gather(). The git numbers live in a separate dict, g["git"], collected ~80 lines LATER in gather() than the status block that would have needed them. Rendered evidence, from the same page: the band says 'Nothing is waiting on you', line2 names only the canon note, and panel p3 four inches below renders `Unpushed3`. Three commits are sitting on the laptop and the page's top line does not know.
findings.user_impact: This is D3 — 'is my last work in front of her, or on my laptop' — failing at the one altitude Paul reads on an 80%-clear visit. Its documented precedent is the exact one CLAUDE.md names: a ribbon Paul wrote and didn't push is exactly as stale to Mom as one he never wrote. And it is the SAME defect the seat-2 spec called critical (F3: 'a green Nothing is waiting on you rendered directly above a Shipping panel with Uncommitted 1 in red') — the rebuild moved it from `Uncommitted` to `Unpushed` rather than removing it. A branch that reads as if it handles the case is worse than one that omits it, because it stops anyone checking — the same trap CLAUDE.md names about the secret-scan's 18 days.
findings.principle_invoked: One engine, one verdict (fernwood.md, paul-ratified) + Nielsen H1 (visibility of system status)
findings.recommendation: In verdict(), stop reading `sig["repo"]` and read `g["git"]` directly — it is already collected and is the page's only source for those numbers: `if g["git"]["unpushed"]: v["notes"].append(("p3", f"{n} unpushed commit(s) — a commit is not a ship"))`, same for `dirty`. Then delete the `sig.get("repo")` lookup so no future reader believes a repo signal exists in that dict. Add one assertion in verdict(): every panel that renders a value in `.bad` must have a corresponding entry in `yours` or `notes` — if that invariant is not machine-checkable, it will break again.

findings.status: CONFIRMED — this is Paul's observed defect, re-diagnosed
findings.observation: The band's line1 is an absolute that line2 retracts. Rendered verbatim: l1 = 'Nothing is waiting on you'; l2 = '7 checks ran · nothing owed at leg 5 · also: viewer inlines or Guru's digest are behind canon'. The page has a genuine two-tier model (yours / notes) and a one-tier vocabulary (CLEAR / YOURS), so the second tier can only be expressed as a footnote beginning 'also:'. Note that the CANT_TELL state already proves the model tolerates a third band — the machinery exists.
findings.user_impact: On the 80% of visits the charter designs for, line1 is the whole page. A line1 that must be read together with line2 to be true is not a glance. Worse for trust than for accuracy: the charter names the page's strongest force as ANXIETY — 'that the page becomes another confident summary that goes quietly stale' — and the first thing Paul actually caught it doing is asserting clear while naming its own exception. One instance of this teaches him to read past line1, which costs the page its only reason to exist.
findings.principle_invoked: Lead with the synthesis, not the rows (cross-project) — the synthesis is the deliverable, and a synthesis with a retraction attached is not one. Plus Norman: the conceptual model the reader builds from 'Nothing is waiting on you' is wrong, and the page taught it to him.
findings.recommendation: Give the second tier its own state and its own word. Three-way on the yours axis: (a) `yours` non-empty → band-YOURS, l1 'N things are yours'; (b) `yours` empty AND `notes` non-empty → NEW `band-NOTED` (pale amber, e.g. #f4efdc on #6a5a20 ink — one new CSS class, one new branch), l1 'Nothing is owed to Mom — N for you'; (c) both empty → band-CLEAR, l1 'Nothing is waiting on you'. Only (c) may use the absolute. This single change also fixes F5 and F6 at the same time, because it moves the exception out of the footnote and into the headline where it belongs.

findings.status: CONFIRMED — and it is the FOURTH occurrence the fernwood principle pre-registered
findings.observation: mom-cycle-status.py:187 decides the same question with a THIRD rule: `if not needs_paul and sig["canon_surfaces"]["clean"] and not sig["repo"]["unpushed_commits"]: print("🟢 Nothing is waiting on you.")`. On today's inputs that tool would NOT print the green line — canon is dirty and there are 3 unpushed commits — while the page prints the identical sentence in 34px. The page itself advertises the disagreement: the Doors panel offers `python3 tools/mom-cycle-status.py` as its 'terminal twin'. Same input set, same output slot, same words, different threshold.
findings.user_impact: The one cross-check Paul is invited to run returns a different verdict than the surface that invited him. That is worse than either being wrong alone: it makes both unreliable, and it lands on the exact reader whose stated anxiety is a confident summary he cannot audit.
findings.principle_invoked: One engine, one verdict — SHARPENING CLAUSE (paul-ratified 2026-08-02): 'the tell is not a shared call — it is a shared INPUT SET plus a shared output slot.' And the file's own pre-registered answer: 'If a fourth appears, the answer is not another reconciliation layer — it is that the two functions should have been one.' Occurrence trail was 07-06 fishing, 07-14 weather, 08-02 weather. This is the fourth, on a third domain.
findings.recommendation: Do what the principle already says. Move the verdict rules INTO mom-cycle-status.py as an exported `verdict(sig) -> {state, line1, line2, yours, notes}`; have mom-cycle-status.main() print it and build-control.verdict() render it. build-control already imports that module via _shim for LEGS and already feeds it this run's exit codes — the plumbing exists. Delete build-control's copy of the rules. Do not add a reconciliation check between the two; that is the layer the principle forbids.

findings.observation: Panel p4 renders `the detectors say — leg 5 — nothing owed`, in green. But position() returns leg 5 for exactly one reason: `if not sig["canon_surfaces"]["clean"]: return "5", False`. The leg number IS the finding, and it is rendered as its own opposite in the affirmative colour, with the reason omitted. Leg 5's name (SHIP) is visible in the list above it, but nothing connects 'we are at 5' to 'because canon surfaces are behind'.
findings.user_impact: D4 ('is a lap open, and where') gets an answer that reads as reassurance. A reader who has learned that leg 7 = CLOSE and leg 6 = GATE has no way to learn that leg 5 means something is wrong, because the one place that could teach him says 'nothing owed' beside it.
findings.principle_invoked: Nielsen H2 (match between system and the real world) — an internal index rendered without its meaning; plus 'A value's provenance must be shown as honestly as the value itself' (the provenance of a leg number is the rule that produced it)
findings.recommendation: Render the reason with the leg, from the same signal that produced it: `leg 5 · SHIP — canon surfaces are behind; nothing is owed to her`. Keep the green only on the 'nothing owed to her' clause, not on the leg. One f-string change in p4_loop, reading `sig` which is already in scope.

findings.status: CONFIRMED — known-unfixed item #2, RE-RANKED UP (nice-to-have → important)
findings.observation: line2 carries three jobs: a coverage denominator ('7 checks ran'), a position ('nothing owed at leg 5'), and an exception ('also: …'). Re-ranking up for two reasons the earlier pass could not have weighed: (a) since the notes tier has no other above-the-fold home (F6), that trailing clause is now the SOLE carrier of the exception, and it is introduced by 'also:', the weakest conjunction in English for a clause that contradicts the sentence before it; (b) in the YOURS state line2 is `" · ".join(t for _p, t in v["yours"])` with no cap — three findings produce an unbroken 17px run-on inside a red block, exactly when reading speed matters most.
findings.user_impact: The one line the reader must parse fastest is the one carrying three unrelated dimensions. 'leg 5' is also an unexplained internal referent at the very top of the page, four panels above the table that decodes it.
findings.principle_invoked: Ordering first, then type in service of it (paul-stated 2026-07-30) — 'organize along the dimension that answers the reader's top question.' Three dimensions in one 17px line is no ordering at all. Plus Make-every-surface-read-at-a-glance, transposed to the expert reader.
findings.recommendation: One job per line. l2 = the exception if one exists, else nothing (an empty l2 is a legitimate and strong state — the band's min-height already holds the shape). Move '7 checks ran' to p5's panel header where the checks are, as its denominator. Delete 'at leg 5' from the band — p4 already carries it, better. In the YOURS state, cap l2 at the two highest-ranked items and append '· +N more below' rather than joining all of them.

findings.observation: The SEE THIS chip renders inside p5's `<h2>`, and p5 is the second section of colA inside `.lower`. Below 1240px — where the two-column media query does not fire — p5 is the FIFTH section down the page. Above 1240px it is still below the three full-width top panels. In the CLEAR state the band is #dff0cf, the palest of the three, so nothing above the fold is marked at all. Separately: p5 orders 'The loop's checks' (all green today) BEFORE 'Canon surfaces' (both red today), so within the panel the news is second as well.
findings.user_impact: The whole notes tier is reachable only by scrolling past the panels that had nothing to say. On a page whose falsifier is 'if Paul reads it end to end and takes no different action, it is decoration,' the tier that names the actions is the one placed furthest from the glance.
findings.principle_invoked: Lead with the synthesis, not the rows (cross-project) + 'Freshness sets altitude' generalized: what CHANGED sets altitude, and today the only things that changed are in the buried tier
findings.recommendation: Add a notes strip immediately under the band, above p1: one line per note, each an anchor to its panel — `SEE THIS  canon surfaces are behind canon → p5` / `SEE THIS  3 unpushed commits → p3`. Amber marks, 13px, no box. It is the same `v["notes"]` list already computed, rendered once at the top instead of only as chips. Do NOT reorder p5's two groups — the grouping is a stable PLACE and Paul learns it ('A menu's order is a PLACE; a worklist's order is a RANKING'); the within-group sort by DID NOT RUN → WANTS YOU → PASSED is already the correct ranking.

findings.status: CONFIRMED — known-unfixed item #1, but RE-DIAGNOSED (the stated problem is the smaller half)
findings.observation: `.priv{background:#5a2222;color:#fff}` — a saturated dark-red filled block, four lines of 12.5px reversed text, immediately above the band. The stated problem is real: in CLEAR the band is pale (#dff0cf) so the banner is the highest-contrast object on the page. But the sharper problem is the OTHER state: in YOURS the band is `var(--red)` #b3402a, also filled, also reversed — so a reader arriving at the page's most consequential state meets two saturated red blocks stacked, and the one that is always there is the one on top. There is no visual rule telling him which red is the news. And the banner's information content is zero on every render: it is identical in all three states and on every run, forever.
findings.user_impact: Salience is the page's scarcest currency and its top slot is permanently allocated to a constant. Two further points argue for demotion beyond aesthetics: (a) the banner's actual reader is Paul, who already knows this file is private — the reader who could ACT wrongly on it is a future agent, and that reader reads the generator docstring, which already carries the warning at greater length; (b) the banner's text over-claims what is on the page (see F14).
findings.principle_invoked: Ornament earns its place (cross-project/form-and-restraint.md) — and its inverse: a signifier that never varies carries no information and must not hold the highest-salience position. Plus Norman on signifier salience mapping to information value.
findings.recommendation: Keep the constraint, drop the shout. One line above the h1, small, in ink with a dark-red left rule (3px #5a2222) and no fill: `PRIVATE · .private/, gitignored · nothing here goes on her surfaces`. Move the full reasoning paragraph to the page footer, beside the existing 'No model ran to produce this page' line — where the other standing statements-of-limits already live, and where it composes with them instead of competing with the verdict. Reserve filled saturated colour on this page for exactly one thing: the band. Charter §3 item 10 says 'keep it' — this keeps it; it demotes the treatment, not the rule.

findings.status: CONFIRMED as a CSS defect — but at a different width band than reported
findings.observation: The breakpoint does not account for the body's padding. `body{padding:22px 18px 60px}` and `@media (min-width:1240px){.wrap{max-width:1240px}}`. The padding sits OUTSIDE .wrap's max-width, so once the query fires the page requires 1240 + 18 + 18 = 1276px. Every viewport from 1240px to 1275px inclusive therefore triggers the wide layout and then overflows horizontally by up to 36px — content clipped on the right, exactly as described. Below 1240px the layout is 900 + 36 = 936px and cannot clip from this cause. So: real bug, 36px-wide failure band, and if Paul's window was literally 1200 CSS px the cause is something else — in which case the next suspects are `table.grid`'s auto layout being forced past 100% by a `<pre class="out">` line with no break opportunity, and the two `<code>` strings in Doors (the `cd …` command and the live URL).
findings.user_impact: A page whose job is a one-minute glance, losing its right edge at a plausible laptop width. Low frequency, high annoyance, near-zero cost to fix.
findings.principle_invoked: Nielsen H5 (error prevention) at the layout level; and the page's own restraint stance — a breakpoint that needs a footnote to be correct is a broken breakpoint
findings.recommendation: Move the horizontal padding off `body` and onto `.wrap`: `body{padding:22px 0 60px}` / `.wrap{max-width:900px;margin:0 auto;padding:0 18px}` (box-sizing is already border-box, so max-width then includes the padding and the breakpoint arithmetic is exact). Belt-and-braces for the second suspect: add `pre.out{overflow-wrap:anywhere}` and `table.grid{table-layout:fixed}`. Then check the actual failure width by dragging the window — if it clips below 1240 after this change, the table is the culprit and `table-layout:fixed` will have caught it.

findings.observation: A red check hands back the command that DIAGNOSES, not the one that acts. Rendered verbatim under the canon drift: `$ python3 tools/check-data-inline.py` — the tool whose output Paul has just finished reading, one line above. Same for the digest: `$ python3 tools/check-digest-fresh.py`. The next moves exist and are written down in CLAUDE.md: `python3 tools/check-data-inline.py --fix` (gated — only after Paul confirms the drift is a legitimate addition, per the canon-ahead rule) and `python3 tools/build-digest.py && (cd worker && npx wrangler deploy)`. Neither appears. Secondary: the command is inside the same `<pre>` as the tool output, so copying it is a careful drag rather than a double-click.
findings.user_impact: The handoff to terminal is INCIDENTAL, not designed, in precisely the case the page exists for. On a clear visit the page saves Paul the terminal block; on the one visit where something is wrong it returns him to the terminal with less than he arrived with — he re-runs a check he has already read.
findings.principle_invoked: A correct 'no' still owes a next move (cross-project/interaction-and-friction.md). The charter's own §6-f says the same thing about the prototype: 'the one case where the page has the most value is the one case it sends him back to the terminal.'
findings.recommendation: Give each check an optional `next` string in LOOP_CHECKS/CANON_CHECKS and render it BELOW the output in its own `.cmd` block, visually separate from the `<pre>`, with the human gate stated where one exists: `next — python3 tools/check-data-inline.py --fix   ⚠ only after you confirm the drift is a real canon addition (CLAUDE.md)`. The gate belongs on the page precisely because the fix is one keystroke and the confirmation is the whole safeguard. Keep the diagnostic command too, below the fix. Separately, move `$ …` out of the `<pre>` so it is a double-click-selectable line.

findings.observation: The Doors panel (p7) is the SECOND item in colB, directly beneath p6 'Her side of the loop' — the longest panel on the page by a wide margin (five sub-tables, three h3 headings, ~250px of `.dim` explanatory prose). Below 1240px, Doors is the seventh of eight sections. Doors carries the live app link, the preview command, the four navigation files, and the one command.
findings.user_impact: The charter names HABIT as a force: 'the page must be cheaper than the habit it replaces.' Doors IS the cheapness — it is the part of the page that replaces typing. Placing it under the page's longest panel taxes exactly the thing that has to be free. Compounding: p6 serves D5 (rank 5) and D6 (rank 6, which the page correctly refuses to answer), so the page's largest object serves its weakest decisions. This is a milder version of the same inversion the seat-2 spec caught (F4: the 14-row backlog scrape outweighing the return leg) — the rebuild fixed the extreme case and left the ordering inside colB unexamined.
findings.principle_invoked: Ordering first, then type in service of it (paul-stated) — surface area is an ordering signal and here it disagrees with the decision ranking. Plus 'Meet the user at the action.'
findings.recommendation: Two-line change in render(): colB order becomes p7 (Doors) → p8 (Open work) → p6 (Her side of the loop). Doors and Open work are both short; putting them first means the long reference panel sinks to the bottom of the column in BOTH layouts, which is where the governing glance-and-repository principle puts a repository. No restyling needed.

findings.observation: Under 'The one command', the page offers `/mom-cycle` — a Claude skill — as the primary, in `<code>` at body size. The deterministic equivalent is demoted to `.dim` sub-text: 'terminal twin: python3 tools/mom-cycle-status.py'. On a page whose generator docstring opens with '⭐ IT IS A NON-AI DOOR' and whose falsifier is 'if the only way to learn whether Mom is owed a reply were to ask Claude, this loop would be broken.'
findings.user_impact: The page is a non-AI door that points at an AI door as the way through. Not a correctness failure — the twin IS named, so the door exists — but the typographic ranking says the opposite of the doctrine. Given the page's other purpose (it is itself a portfolio artifact of a governed loop), the ranking is the visible claim.
findings.principle_invoked: Deterministic things need a non-AI door (global CLAUDE.md, paul-stated 2026-08-02) + Ordering first, then type in service of it — the type here contradicts the ordering the doctrine sets
findings.recommendation: Invert. `python3 tools/mom-cycle-status.py` at body size as the primary; `/mom-cycle` beside it, same size, labelled for what it is: 'the assisted run — the full lap, with the gates.' Both are legitimate; they are just ranked backwards. Retitle the block from 'The one command' to 'Two ways in' — there are two, and the page saying 'one' is what forced the ranking.

findings.status: CONFIRMED — this is my answer to the clock-taxonomy question
findings.observation: Three of the four clocks earn their cost; one does not. EVENT, PROBE and COMMIT each mark a genuinely different denominator (her actions / the network / git), they are the direct descendant of the rainfall-card lesson Paul validated in his own words, and the page relies on them to keep 'her last visit 3d' from being read against 'HEAD 21h'. Keep all three. GEN does not. It appears in five panel headers, in every case reading 'GEN 0m', and it is BY CONSTRUCTION always identical to the page's own age — which the page already declares at the top, in words, recomputed live at view time ('this page is N minutes old'). Five repetitions of a value the reader has already been given, in a slot he must learn to skip.
findings.user_impact: Small, but it is the page's own restraint standard: five labels that never vary and never disagree with a number already on screen. Removing it also strengthens the remaining three by making a clock label mean 'this one is on a different clock than the page' — which is the only reason to label a clock at all.
findings.principle_invoked: Ornament earns its place (cross-project/form-and-restraint.md) — the redundancy clause. Plus the page's own footer thesis: labels exist so the reader can tell which clock a number is on; GEN is the default and needs no name.
findings.recommendation: Drop `GEN {elapsed(...)}` from the five panel headers; a panel with no clock label is on the page's clock, which the top line states. Reduce the footer legend to three terms and add the default explicitly: 'unlabelled = this build; EVENT (something of hers) · PROBE (the network) · COMMIT (git).' Do not touch EVENT/PROBE/COMMIT — a generic reviewer would 'simplify' all four into one 'updated N ago' and that would reintroduce the rainfall-card error Mom herself caught.

findings.observation: The document title is `● Fernwood control` in the CLEAR state and would be identical on a run with no notes at all — the title map has three entries (▲ YOURS / ● CLEAR / — CANT_TELL) for a model that, after F2, has four states. The title is the tab-strip glance and today's tab says all-clear while two checks are red.
findings.user_impact: Minor on its own; it matters because a background tab is how a control page is actually kept, and the tab is the only surface that survives being scrolled away from.
findings.principle_invoked: An artifact must carry its own status in its pixels (cross-project/honest-surfaces.md) — the tab is a pixel surface
findings.recommendation: Add the fourth entry when F2 lands: `◐ Fernwood control — N for you`. One dict key.

findings.observation: The PRIVATE banner states the page 'Carries her engagement counts, her last visit and open work.' It no longer carries open work — p8 was correctly reduced to a pointer and a mtime, with no rows and no count. The banner's claim is a leftover from the version it was written for.
findings.user_impact: Trivial in consequence, non-trivial in class: this is a hand-maintained sentence describing a generated surface, drifting in the direction that flatters the sentence. It is the same shape as the '~4,600 lines' architecture note that read wrong for months. On this page of all pages it should not survive a review.
findings.principle_invoked: Hand-maintained FACTS drift; DECISIONS don't (memory feedback_hand_maintained_facts_drift) — a standing description of variable content is a fact, not a decision
findings.recommendation: Cut 'and open work'. principles_to_propose.principle: A summary that needs an exception has already failed as a summary — restate it, never append to it. If a headline is followed by 'but', 'also', or 'except', the headline is wrong for that state and the state needs its own words.
principles_to_propose.rationale: 1 occurrence — this review, F2. The page has a genuine two-tier model and a one-tier vocabulary, so the second tier can only ever surface as a footnote that retracts the headline. The failure is guaranteed by the words, not by the logic, which is why it survived a four-seat run that fixed the logic. Candidate; watch for a second occurrence on the financial dashboard's claim-graph verdicts or the operating-layer render, both of which have latent second tiers.

principles_to_propose.principle: A signifier that never varies must not hold the highest-salience position. Reserve the loudest treatment on a surface for the thing that changes; render standing constraints in the register of a rule, not the register of news.
principles_to_propose.rationale: 1 occurrence — this review, F7. Sharpens 'Ornament earns its place' along an axis it does not currently cover: the banner is neither ornament nor untrue, it is a true constant occupying the slot the variable needs. The tell is cheap and general — if an element is byte-identical on every render, it cannot be the loudest thing on the page. Candidate.
